newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia backs Fiji's return to Commonwealth.
newsitem.headline: Australia backs Fiji's return to Commonwealth.

text.p: Australia, embroiled in a diplomatic row with its Pacific neighbours, on Wednesday endorsed Fiji's return to the Commonwealth.

Foreign Minister Alexander Downer said in a radio interview the leading South Pacific nation should be readmitted into the club of former British colonies after it adopted a less racially-based constitution.
Downer said the Australian government believed "that it would be appropriate for Fiji to be re-admitted to the Commonwealth".
Fiji was ejected from the Commonwealth in 1987 after declaring itself a republic following a second military coup.

It passed a constitution in 1990 setting aside parliamentary seats on the basis of race and guaranteeing a majority for ethnic Fijians. A new constitution allowing for a multi-racial government will become law in Fiji on Friday.
Fijian Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka said earlier this year his nation might reapply for Commonwealth membership at the group's heads of government meeting in Scotland in October.

Canberra is under fire from Pacific leaders, including Rabuka, over the publication of a secret government assessment critical of regional economies and the foibles of some South Pacific ministers and leaders.
